content: In December 2017, a comprehensive and costed multisectoral national plan of action was developed to address the issue of child marriage. This plan was designed to provide a structured and integrated response to the problem. The creation of this plan, along with the National End Child Marriage Strategy, was supported technically by the United Nations Global Programme to Accelerate Action to End Child Marriage. Both documents align with the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on preventing early pregnancy and poor reproductive outcomes among adolescents in developing countries. Two pilot districts were chosen for the initial implementation of the multisectoral action plan. Furthermore, the National Assembly of Zambia, in collaboration with the Inter-Parliamentary Union, organized a parliamentary seminar focused on child, early, and forced marriage. During this seminar, a list of actionable steps was identified for parliamentarians to take a more active role in the national implementation process. These steps included approving and supporting relevant legislation, providing oversight, allocating budgets, and representing the issue effectively.
